headline: Relational and longitudinal modelling of brain structure and amyloid dynamics
label: Brain Morphometry And Dynamics
summary: Methods now quantify brain morphology and amyloid-β progression across lifespan, disease, and genetic axes without relying on single-region summaries.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is the characterization of brain structure and its change over time through relational or dynamical structure, rather than single-region summaries. Persistent-homology pipelines for T1 MRI avoid template normalization and are tested on synthetic lesions and ADNI Alzheimer's versus control data. LNODE models regional amyloid-β PET dynamics as a neural ODE with few parameters per subject, jointly calibrated on ADNI and A4 cohorts, and frames progression as a shared spatiotemporal structure. A decision-tree framework identifies feature-specific cortical ageing transitions from 18 to 94 years and relates them to structural covariance network organisation. A fourth item examines how epoch-specific checkpoints of a 3D autoencoder trained on UK Biobank brain MRIs capture distinct genetic architectures of brain morphology. The items differ in modality, question, and data, so the shared element is methodological. What is new is the emphasis on transitions and trajectories as the object of analysis.
